title: AI Attacks Enter New Era as Hackers Use Deepfakes and Automation to Scale Deception
content_md: Cybercriminals are using artificial intelligence to make attacks faster and deception harder to spot. AI agents can carry out parts of an intrusion with limited human direction, while deepfake voices and video can make a fraudulent request appear to come from a trusted executive. Recent cases show different uses of AI rather than one universal attack method. In a campaign disclosed by Anthropic in November 2025, a group it identified as GTG-1002 used Claude Code to support cyber espionage against roughly 30 organizations. Anthropic assessed the group with high confidence as Chinese state-sponsored. Its report says the AI performed about 80% to 90% of the tactical work, while human operators made a small number of key decisions. Deepfake AI Attacks Scale Deception The AI-assisted work included reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential harvesting and analysis of stolen data. That does not mean the attack ran without people, operators selected targets and approved important steps. It does show how automation can let attackers test and pursue several targets with far less hands-on effort. AI is also appearing inside malware. In February 2026, ESET described PromptSpy, Android malware that uses Google’s Gemini to interpret screen elements and guide actions that keep the malicious app in the device’s recent-app list.
